locator.section: 9.3 Aldehydes and ketones, 'Alicyclic ketones' (lower arrow labelled alpha)

evidence.curator_note: Substrate named by the prose ON THIS PAGE: 'Alicyclic ketones. The mass spectrum of 3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexanone (Figure 8.5) illustrates major additional fragmentation pathways found for cyclic ketones (Equation 9.30); these are similar to those discussed for cyclic alcohols and in Section 8.9.' Drawn as a cyclohexanone with '+.' over the oxygen, gem-dimethyl at the lower-left ring carbon and a single methyl at the lower-right one, labelled 'm/z 140'. ATOM MAPS use the ring numbering of that name: 1 = the carbonyl carbon, 2 and 6 = the two alpha CH2 groups, 3 = the gem-dimethyl quaternary carbon, 4 = the remaining ring CH2, 5 = the CH bearing the single methyl, 7 = O, 8/9 = the two 3,3-methyls, 10 = the 5-methyl, 11 = the hydrogen the page draws EXPLICITLY inside the lower ring-opened product, on C6. THIS IS THE OTHER alpha CHANNEL: the lower arrow cleaves C1-C2, not C1-C6, so the acylium ends up attached to C6 and the primary radical sits on C2 -- the page prints the dot on the upper-LEFT ring carbon here, mirroring the upper branch. The two channels are the two symmetry-distinct alpha bonds of the ring, and the 'alpha' MØD rule finds exactly these two (see the mechanism-level note). *** BOND ORDER MEASURED, NOT EYEBALLED: every C-O bond drawn in equation 9.30 is a TRIPLE bond. *** A dark-run pixel profile across the three C-O bonds on the native 1760x2560 scan returns three parallel strokes in each case (upper alpha product at native x 587/598/608, lower at 591/601/611, m/z 83 ion at 1402/1412/1422). At page-render resolution the upper one reads as a double bond, which would make its carbon a sextet; it is not. The ring-opened species are therefore true acylium ions R-C#O+, encoded '[O+:7]#[C:1]' as in IMS9-EQ9.27a. The alpha arrow: the molecular ion carries ZERO arcs (only '+.' over the oxygen), so all three moves are curator-supplied -- the canonical radical-site triple: <1> the oxygen odd electron into the C1-O bond, raising C=O to the C#O+ of the acylium, <2> one electron of the breaking ring bond into that same bond, <3> the second electron staying on the departing ring carbon as the new radical site. The ring does not fall apart: the 'fragments' stay tied together through the rest of the ring, so this step is a RING OPENING to a distonic ion of unchanged mass (140.1196), which is why the page draws the product with the same hexagonal layout minus one bond.

locator.section: 9.3 Aldehydes and ketones, 'Alicyclic ketones' (lower arrow labelled 'rH')

evidence.curator_note: The lower 'rH' arrow. Book draws 2 arcs, both SOLID here (this branch carries no competing channel, so nothing is dashed): one from the radical dot on C2 and one from the C6-H bond, their heads CONVERGING on the gap between C2 and the explicitly drawn H -- measured at 5x, the convergence point sits at the midpoint of the forming C2-H bond. Moves <1,2> are those arcs; move <3>, not drawn, leaves the second C6-H electron on C6 as the new radical site, which the page then prints on the next structure. After the transfer C2 is a methyl on the gem-dimethyl carbon -- the page redraws that end as a tert-butyl group, which is the check that the H landed where this record puts it.

locator.section: 9.3 Aldehydes and ketones, 'Alicyclic ketones' (lower arrow labelled alpha, to m/z 69)

evidence.curator_note: The final 'alpha' arrow. Book draws 2 arcs on the rearranged ion: one from the radical dot on C6 into the C5-C6 bond, one from the C4-C5 bond into the same bond; move <3> (the second C4-C5 electron staying on C4) is not drawn but is what produces the printed neutral radical. PRODUCTS AS DRAWN: the ion is the conjugated acylium O+#C-CH=CH-CH3 labelled 'm/z 69' (C4H5O+, 69.0335 -- note this is the OXYGEN-containing 69, not the C5H9+ hydrocarbon at 69.0699 that the same nominal mass could mean), and the neutral is drawn as a four-line vertex with a dot on one branch, i.e. the NEOPENTYL radical .CH2-C(CH3)3 (C5H11., 71.0861). The two sum to 140.1196. MEASUREMENTS (convention F): the page LABELS m/z 140, 112, 56, 83 and 69 on the scheme itself, and every one of them matches the exact mass computed from the structure encoded here (140.1196, 112.1247, 56.0621, 83.0491, 69.0335 -- RDKit ExactMolWt, which already applies the formal charge). Peak assignments store those computed exact masses with status 'proposed', the corpus convention for a book-labelled m/z (IMS9-EQ9.22, IMS9-EQ9.19a). NO relative_intensity: the scheme prints no percentage, and Figure 8.5 -- the actual 3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexanone spectrum, which does carry abundances -- is in chapter 8, not on this page.

data/mechanisms/rule_index.json has NO chapter-9 entries. *** VERIFIED POSITIVE CROSS-LINK for the alpha step (RDKit-tested, not asserted): 'alpha' (src/data_generation/rules/wikipedia.py:6, '[C]1[C]2({=}[O+.])[C]3[C]4 >> [C]1[C]2{#}[O+].[C.]3[C]4') embeds EXACTLY TWICE on this molecular ion, at (C2,C1,O7,C6,C5) and (C6,C1,O7,C2,C3). *** Those two embeddings are precisely the two alpha channels the page draws -- the upper branch cleaving C1-C6 and the lower one cleaving C1-C2 -- so the rule set finds the branch point independently of the drawing, and its RHS gives the acylium plus carbon radical encoded here, including raising C=O to C#O+. It is live via wiki_fragmentation -> 'fragmentation' (rules/__init__.py:48). TESTED AND REJECTED for the later steps: 'aryl_CO_loss' (aromatic_ring_loss.py:49) gives 0 embeddings on the acylium (it is an aromatic ring-contraction rule, LHS needs a phenol), and 'hTransition_unsaturated_alpha' (IMS_bookCover.py:50) gives 0 on the rH product (its LHS requires the protonated [_A+][H] enol form, not an acylium). No rule was found or tested for the CO loss or the rH steps themselves: UNTESTED, not 'no rule matches'.
